solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Summary is not quite accurate

indicators.note: not quite means the word for accurate falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: precise means accurate

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a summary they were given is slightly off the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a brief written abstract giving the main points of a longer text.

clue.text: PM's diary sets out high points of NE African tour

definitions.text: high points of NE African tour

indicators.note: sets out means the letters are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters P, M and S as printed, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's diary lists the highlights of an official tour of north-east Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pyramids at Giza are the classic sights on a tour of north-east Africa, and literally tall peaked structures.

clue.text: Cries on seeing awful climaxes

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of the next word are in a dreadful mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out in dismay at the dreadful endings of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to call out suddenly, so cries and exclaims are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Risk including a kind of measure

indicators.note: including means the first word's synonym holds the next piece within it

parts.note: to imperil something is to risk or endanger it

explanation.surface: A statement that a gamble involves some kind of yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial units such as feet, pounds and gallons form the traditional British system of weights and measures.

clue.text: Something helpful that may get you into Oxford

definitions.text: Something helpful that may get you into Oxford

parts.words: Something helpful that may get you into Oxford
parts.note: an Oxford is also a style of laced leather shoe, and a curved tool helps a foot slide into one

explanation.surface: Advice about whatever aid might win you a place at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests university admission; an Oxford here is a laced shoe, which this tool helps the heel slip into.
explanation.definitionFit: This curved implement eases a heel into a tight shoe such as an Oxford brogue.

clue.text: Saw distress in her cable

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters sit inside the word that follows
distress as a verb means to damage or batter, so the letters of the word before are knocked about

explanation.surface: A ship's cable that someone saw her struggling with in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Not the genuine article from bankers at Zurich

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A warning that something offered by Swiss bankers is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes a substitute or imitation, an inferior replacement for the real thing.

clue.text: Possibly tore in from the east

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of the following words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something perhaps ripped its way in, coming from the eastern side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old name for the countries of the East, especially eastern Asia.

clue.text: Almost a point too soon

parts.note: N, north, is one point of the compass
early means ahead of time, too soon

explanation.surface: A remark that someone arrived a fraction ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are adverb synonyms meaning not quite completely.

clue.text: Kitchener's formula for success?

parts.note: Kitchener suggests the British field marshal, but here means anyone working in a kitchen, whose formula is a list of ingredients and method

explanation.surface: Asks what Lord Kitchener, the British war leader, used as his formula for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was a famous British field marshal; read the name as 'kitchen worker' and the formula becomes a cooking method.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook follows written instructions for a dish, a culinary formula that ensures it turns out well.

clue.text: Many Nazis were armed with this

definitions.text: Many Nazis were armed with this

parts.words: Many Nazis were armed with this
parts.note: armed suggests weapons, but the hooked cross on Nazi armbands literally has four bent arms

explanation.surface: A sombre statement about the weapons carried by German soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed' points to guns, but the emblem has arms of its own and was worn on armbands.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked cross was the Nazi party emblem, worn on armbands and itself built from four bent arms.

clue.text: Many agree it's new and in short supply

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

indicators.note: new means the letters of the word before are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Plenty of people concur that something novel is scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lacking in quantity, so it describes something in short supply.

clue.text: Guard dispatched one with a half-nelson

parts.note: sent means dispatched
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: half means only the first three letters of the following six-letter word are used

explanation.surface: A wrestler sent off a guard by putting him in a half-nelson hold.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-nelson is a wrestling hold; here 'half' just halves the word nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or watchman posted to keep guard.

clue.text: A land is devastated by ancient Muslim warrior

indicators.note: devastated means the letters of the preceding words are laid waste and rearranged

explanation.surface: A country is laid waste by a medieval Muslim commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan who led Muslim forces against the Crusaders.

clue.text: Pitch of the road

parts.note: pitch could mean slope or gradient of a road, but here it is the black sticky substance used to surface roads

explanation.surface: A question about how steeply a road slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is a dark viscous pitch spread on roads as a surfacing material.

clue.text: Humble cleric takes me in

indicators.note: takes, with in, means the cleric's title receives the next word inside it
in completes the instruction that the following word goes inside

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A modest churchman offers someone shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to humble or lower them in dignity, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Get neither number right

explanation.surface: Someone fails to get either figure correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by pairing: the answer is the word that goes with neither.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction is the partner of neither, as in 'neither here ... there', completing the negative pair.

clue.text: For the returning traveller

indicators.note: returning means the word for a traveller is read back the other way

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: Something set aside for someone coming home from a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head', so it can stand for 'for'.

clue.text: Places drawn roughly to scale

indicators.note: drawn roughly suggests a sketch done carelessly, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sketch map shows sites in approximately the right proportions.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate is to find or position something, so places and locates are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Examination on this writer I don't know

parts.note: a search is a thorough examination
this writer means the setter, me

explanation.surface: A test is set on the author, who professes ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an informal idiom meaning I have no idea.

clue.text: Guard the stupid girl

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of the preceding words are senseless as given and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A command to protect a foolish young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, a girl in relation to her parents.

clue.text: He's crazy to pocket ball at end of break

indicators.note: at end of places the snooker term after the word for a fracture

parts.note: a crack is a break or fracture
to pot is to strike a ball into a pocket in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A snooker player is mad to sink a ball at the close of his run of shots.
explanation.walkthrough: A break in snooker is a scoring run of shots; here it just means a fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, matching the description of someone who is mad.

clue.text: Go about two

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pair is two

explanation.surface: A terse instruction for a couple to circle round.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal way of saying to go there.

clue.text: It's not just perfume that's upset and left

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for perfume is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: an aroma is a fragrance or perfume

explanation.surface: Someone complains that it is more than mere scent that has spilled and gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely', but in the definition it means fair or righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking moral standards, so something amoral is not righteous or fair.

clue.text: The whole country is full of conservationists

indicators.note: is full of means the country's name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: An entire nation is packed with environmental campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means complete, all of something, so it can replace the whole.

clue.text: False alibi initially excluded by Scottish magistrate

indicators.note: false means the letters of the following word are not genuine as given and must be rearranged
initially means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A Scottish judge throws out a fake alibi.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a bailie is a town councillor serving as a local magistrate.

clue.text: A bird that is after quiet

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for that is following the quiet sign

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A bird that comes along once things go quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie is an old word for the magpie, a black and white crow.

clue.text: I creep around and force a way in

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the preceding words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A burglar describes sneaking round a house before breaking in.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to puncture or penetrate, forcing a way into something.

clue.text: Chinese fruit

definitions.meaning: a high official of imperial China, and the main Chinese language
a small loose-skinned orange, like a tangerine

explanation.surface: A simple label for an orange-like fruit from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is both the chief Chinese language and a small citrus fruit.

clue.text: Unfortunate soldier trapped in reversing vehicle

indicators.note: trapped in means the soldier sits inside the other piece
reversing means the word for a vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a soldier pinned by a reversing truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means disastrous or very unlucky, a stronger version of unfortunate.

clue.text: Mocking bird with tips of tail blue or grey

parts.note: a rail is a wading bird, such as the water rail

indicators.note: tips of here means the ends, the final letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A mockingbird described by its blue or grey tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mocking bird' runs together as a species name, but the definition is just 'Mocking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or ridicule, the act of mocking someone.

clue.text: Reduced to silence when imprisoned

explanation.surface: A prisoner was gagged once locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both silenced and confined, as a prisoner is locked in a cell.

clue.text: Chaps from Belgium are loyal subjects

parts.note: Liège is a city in Belgium, so its people come from Belgium
men means chaps

explanation.surface: Belgian men are described as faithful citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times liegemen were vassals bound to serve their lord, hence faithful followers.

clue.text: From around the globe I ruthlessly acquire capital

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A ruthless tycoon boasts of grabbing money from all over the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon.
